+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: 8c80
+title: 'Multitool: correct the stale ToolMount.defaultWaitSeconds references'
+---
+## What
+Cross-repo task in `../FoundationModelsMultitool`. Found while I did the `Parked`/`Elevation` rename of ^t73m7pw.
+
+`IntegrationTests/Tests/FoundationModelsMultitoolIntegrationTests/Fixtures/ScenarioTools.swift` says the deep-scan delay sits "between the two clocks Router's native session mount arms a `runCode` call with (`ToolMount.synchronous`): longer than its 5-second `defaultWaitSeconds`".
+
+Router deleted `ToolMount.defaultWaitSeconds`. `ToolMount.synchronous` is now `ToolMount(mode: .runToCompletion, timeout: defaultTimeoutSeconds)`, one clock of 120 seconds and no wait window. So the sentence names a symbol that does not exist and describes a two-clock design that is gone.
+
+It was out of the scope of ^t73m7pw: `rg 'waitSeconds'` does not match `defaultWaitSeconds`, so neither acceptance criterion of that card covered it.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] `rg -i 'defaultWaitSeconds' Sources Tests IntegrationTests` in FoundationModelsMultitool returns no match.
+- [ ] The prose beside `integrationDeepScanDelay` states the clock the mount really arms, and states why the delay sits below it.
+- [ ] `swift test` green, and `swift build --build-tests --package-path IntegrationTests --disable-automatic-resolution` clean.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] Documentation only; no new behavior. Run the suites before and after.
+
+## Workflow
+- Read `ToolMount.swift` in `../FoundationModelsRouter` first, and state the real clock. #cleanup #docs
\ No newline at end of file
